01cec0e5df.q: How does Komie Haghighi build an elite coaching practice without social media presence?
01cec0e5df.a: Komie attracts top-level clients—business owners and famous individuals—through referrals and word-of-mouth rather than social media. He works on a one-to-one basis with VIP clients only at The Nest retreat center in Costa Rica, using his breathwork methodology and psychological expertise to facilitate life transformations without relying on public social platforms.
01cec0e5df.e: Why Everything in Life Is Sales — Komie Haghighi
01cec0e5df.rq: To care. To actually put the person's need before yourself. Having more or anything else is coming from a place of authenticity and doing what you're doing not just because you think it's going to make you a buck but because it's something you genuinely enjoy doing.

d2cb872018.q: How does Komie Haghighi use breathwork and pattern recognition to accelerate psychological transformation?
d2cb872018.a: Komie identifies core emotional patterns—shame, guilt, doubt, worry—that originate from trauma or past failures and permeate all areas of life. Rather than 20 years of traditional therapy, he works with the energy associated with the problem directly. By helping clients shift from feeling unsafe to feeling powerful, he achieves in 10 hours what conventional therapy might take 20 years to accomplish, because addressing the root energy eliminates the pattern everywhere it manifests.

ed704f57e4.q: What did Komie Haghighi learn from telephone sales at age 17 about confidence and persuasion?
ed704f57e4.a: At 17, while doing high-volume phone sales, Komie learned from a mentor named Elvis to use his voice, stand tall, and project his personality with confidence. He realized that ultimately people buy from the person, not the product. By having faith in what you are saying, the person on the other end will buy into whatever you are selling them.

2f0bf83824.q: Why does Komie Haghighi emphasize creating desire over pointing out mistakes in coaching?
2f0bf83824.a: Komie believes negative feedback reinforces what not to do (like saying 'I am not safe' reinforces the absence of safety). Instead, he recommends preemptively focusing on what to create—like generating desire in a conversation. By introducing an overriding positive energy, the person's attention shifts away from mistakes, and they naturally embody the desired behavior without resistance.
